extracted.intended_audience: B Corps, brand/marketing/communications teams, and organizations interested in B Corp certification
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes 2023 survey findings about public awareness and perceptions of the B Corp Certification in the U.S. and Canada and provides actionable recommendations for B Corps to grow brand recognition and influence purchasing behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlighting B Corp Certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlighting B Corp Certification can help a company stand out in a crowded field of certifications and develop deeper trust with consumers—especially younger ones who increasingly factor in a company’s environmental and social commitment when making purchases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use certification visibility as a differentiator in communications and packaging; leverage the certification to build trust and to signal social/environmental commitment. The article cites survey evidence that strong awareness and knowledge of the B Corp brand influences consumer action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification labeling / B Corp logo on product
rubrics_metrics.description: The study found that consumers who recognized the B Corp brand most frequently recalled seeing the logo on a product; certification labeling is a key differentiator for B Corps aiming to connect with an engaged audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the B Corp logo on products and packaging as a primary means of consumer recall; labeling is presented as the most effective way to communicate certification near the point of purchase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand awareness level (percent aware)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our 2023 survey found that 36% of U.S. adults and 35% of Canadian adults were aware of the B Corp brand name or logo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track percent-aware metrics as a baseline for brand recognition; the briefing also notes that about one-third of aware adults reported recommending a product because of its B Corp Certification, indicating awareness can translate to advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Millennial and Gen Z awareness / target demographic
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents ages 18 to 39 had the highest awareness of the B Corp brand (51% in the U.S. and 47% in Canada), while adults 40+ had lower awareness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize outreach to Millennials and Gen Z, who are more likely to use values to shape purchase behavior and are more aware of certifications. Use messaging channels and storytelling that resonate with younger audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived impact, trust, and rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Among those aware of B Corp Certification, 63% of U.S. adults and 71% of Canadian adults believe the certification is making a positive impact; 80% of U.S. adults reported believing standards are somewhat, very, or extremely rigorous; 81% reported some-to-high trust in the certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize the certification’s rigor and impact in communications to reinforce trust. Use survey claims about perceived rigor and impact when positioning certification value to consumers and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top motivators and barriers to purchase
rubrics_metrics.description: Top motivators in the U.S. were “It helps make a difference” (62%) and “Better for the environment” (61%); the top reported barrier was price (“I think they will be more expensive”) at 47%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame messaging around primary motivators (difference-making, environmental benefits) while proactively addressing price perceptions—e.g., communicate value, affordability, or long-term benefits to mitigate the price barrier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social issues associated with B Corp Certification
rubrics_metrics.description: When asked which social issues are important to a B Corp, U.S. respondents reported fair business practices (63%), sustainability/climate change (60%), access to healthcare (60%), and racial equity/anti-racism (58%) as most connected to B Corp values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight these themes (fair business practices, sustainability, healthcare access, racial equity) in brand narratives and impact storytelling, especially when targeting younger audiences who rate such issues as highly important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recall sources: product labeling and social media
rubrics_metrics.description: Of respondents aware of the B Corp Certification, most reported seeing the B Corp logo and/or name on a product (49% in the U.S., 45% in Canada); social media was the second-highest place of recall (34% U.S., 33% Canada).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use both product labeling and social media as complementary channels: labels to influence at point-of-purchase and social media to increase visibility and storytelling reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications action — Tell stakeholders and use logo broadly
rubrics_metrics.description: First, let the world know! Tell your customers, suppliers, community, and consumers how and why your company certified, and include the logo on your packaging and all your brand properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement broad, multi-stakeholder communications campaigns that consistently display the B Corp logo across packaging, websites, marketing materials, and partner channels to maximize recall and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications action — Incorporate B Corp journey into brand narrative (impact storytelling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate your B Corp journey into your brand narrative. These storytelling moments are essential in a brand’s overall identity, and a key deciding factor at the point of sale, especially for Millennials and Gen Z. Impact storytelling is vital in transforming our economic system and building better businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use narrative-driven content that explains why the company pursued certification, the impact achieved, and concrete examples—position stories to influence purchase decisions, particularly for younger consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications action — Participate in B Corp Month / collective storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: March is B Corp Month, an annual campaign where our community celebrates everything it means to be a B Corp. Join forces during B Corp Month with 8,000+ B Corps around the world to leverage the power of collective storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate marketing and storytelling efforts with broader community campaigns (e.g., B Corp Month) to amplify reach and benefit from collective momentum and shared messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey methodology and interpretation cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodology: A web-based survey of U.S. and Canadian individuals was drawn from a pool of non-random panel members. Data were weighted to be generalizable to the population. Canadian and U.S. adults were weighted separately and thus are reported separately. Select subgroup splits are shown for U.S. adults only due to sample size limitations for Canadian respondents. Fielding Dates: 8/22/23–9/1/23.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret findings with awareness of methodological limitations (non-random panel, weighting changes); note that question wording and ordering changed in 2023 to align with B Lab Global, making 2023 a baseline for future tracking.
